source_text: Ἀκούσατε δέ, πῶς καὶ περὶ τῶν κηρυξάντων τὴν διδαχὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ μηνυσάντων τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν προεῤῥέθη, τοῦ προειρημένου προφήτου καὶ βασιλέως οὕτως εἰπόντος διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος· „Ἡμέρα τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐρεύγεται ῥῆμα, καὶ νὺξ τῇ νυκτὶ ἀναγγέλλει γνῶσιν. Οὐκ εἰσὶ λαλιαὶ οὐδὲ λόγοι, ὧν οὐχὶ ἀκούονται αἱ φωναὶ αἰτῶν. Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτῶν καὶ εἰς τὰ πέρατα τῆς οἰκουμένης τὰ ῥήματα αἰτῶν. Ἐν τῷ ἡλίῳ ἔθετο τὸ σκήνωμα αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτός, ὡς νυμφίος ἐκπορευόμενος ἐκ παστοῦ αἰτοῦ, ἀγαλλιάσεται ὡς γίγας δραμεῖν ὁδόν“. Πρὸς τούτοις δὲ καὶ λόγων ἑτέρων τῶν προφητευθέντων δι᾿ αἰτοῦ τοῦ Δαυῒδ καλῶς ἔχον καὶ οἰκείως ἐπιμνησθῆναι λελογίσμεθα, ἐξ ὧν μαθεῖν ὑμῖν πάρεστι, πῶς προτρέπεται ζῆν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα, καὶ πῶς μηνύει τὴν γεγενημένην Ἡρώδου τοῖ βασιλέως Ἰουδαίων καὶ αἰτῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ Πιλάτου τοῖ ὑμετέρου παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς γενομένου ἐπιτρόπου σὺν τοῖς αὐτοῦ στρατιώταις κατὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ συνέλευσιν, καὶ ὅτι πιστεύεσθαι ἔμελλεν ὑπὸ τῶν ἐκ παντὸς γένους ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ὅτι αὐτὸν υἱὸν καλεῖ ὁ θεὸς καὶ ὑποτάσσειν αὐτῷ πάντας ἐχθροὺς ἐπήγγελται, καὶ πῶς οἱ δαίμονες, ὅσον ἐπ᾿ αἰτοῖς, τήν τε τοῦ πατρὸς πάντων καὶ δεσπότου θεοῦ καὶ τὴν αἰτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐξουσίαν φυγεῖν πειρῶνται, καὶ ὡς εἰς μετάνοιαν καλεῖ πάντας ὁ θεὸς πρὶν ἐλθεῖν τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς κρίσεως. Εἰρηνται δὲ οὕτως· „Μακάριος ἀνήρ, ὃς οὐκ ἐπορεύθη ἐν βουλῇ ἀσεβῶν καὶ ἐν ὁδῷ ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἔστη καὶ ἐπὶ καθέδραν λοιμῶν οὐκ ἐκάθισεν, ἀλλ᾿ ἢ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ κυρίου τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ αἰτοῦ μελετήσει ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός. Καὶ ἔσται ὡς τὸ ξύλον τὸ πεφυτευμένον παρὰ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὑδάτων, ὃ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ δώσει ἐν καιρῷ αἰτοῦ, καὶ τὸ φύλλον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἀποῤῥυήσεται, καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἂν ποιῇ κατευοδωθήσεται. Οὐχ οὕτως οἱ ἀσεβεῖς, οὐχ οὕτως, ἀλλ᾿ ἤ ὡσεὶ χνοῦς, ὃν ἐκρίπτει ὁ ἄνεμος ἀπο προσώπου τῆς γῆς· διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἀναστήσονται ἀσεβεῖς ἐν κρίσει οὐδὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐν βουλῇ δικαίων, ὅτι γινώσκει κύριος ὁδὸν δικαίων, καὶ ὁδὸς ἀσεβῶν ἀπολεῖται“. „Ινα τί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη. καὶ λαοὶ ἐμελέτησαν καινά; (??)αρέστησαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς, καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ κατὰ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ κατὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ, λέγοντες· Διαῤῥήξωμεν τοὺς δεσμοὺς αἰ τῶν καὶ ἀποῤῥίψωμεν ἀφ᾿ ἡμῶν τὸν ζυγὸν αὐτῶν. Ὁ κατοικῶν ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἐκγελάσεται αὐτούς. καὶ ὁ κύριος ἐκμυκτηριεῖ αὐτούς· τότε λαλήσει πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἐν ὀργῇ αὑτοῦ, καὶ ἐν τῷ θυμῷ αὐτοῦ ταράξει αὐτούς. Ἐγὼ δὲ κατεστάθην βασιλεὺς ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ Σιὼν ὄρος τὸ ἅγιον αὐτοῦ, διαγγέλλων τὸ πρόσταγμα κυρίου. Κύριος εἷπε πρός με· Υἱός μσυ εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε. Αἴτησαι παρ᾿ ἐμοῦ, καὶ δώσω σοι ἔθνη κληρονομίαν σου, καὶ τὴν κατάχεσίν σου τὰ πέρατα τῆς γῆς· ποιμανεῖς αὐτοὺς ἑν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ, ὡς σκεύη κεραμέως συντρίψεις αὐτοὺς. Καὶ νῦν βασιλεῖς σύνετε, παιδεύθητε πάντες οἱ κρίνοντες τὴν γῆν. Δουλεύσατε τῷ κυρίῳ ἐν φόβῳ, καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε αὐτῷ ἐν τρ(??)μῳ. Δράξασθε παιδείας, μή ποτε ὀργισθῇ κύριος, καὶ ἀπολεῖσθε ἐξ ὁδοῦ δικαίας, ὅταν ἐκκαυθῇ ἐν τάχει ὁ θυμὸς αὐτοῦ. Μακάριοι πάντες οἱ πεποιθότες ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν“.
pass_a_gloss: Hear, how also concerning the ones having preached his teaching and having announced his epiphany, it was spoken beforehand by the aforementioned prophet and king, thus speaking through the prophetic spirit: Day to day utters a word, and night to night announces knowledge. There are no speeches or words, of which the voices of those who ask are not heard. Into all the earth their sound has gone out and into the ends of the inhabited world their words. He has set his tabernacle in the sun, and he, like a groom coming out of his chamber, will rejoice like a giant to run a course. In addition to these things, we have also thought it right to recall other words of those prophesied through the Spirit of David, from which you can learn how the prophetic Spirit exhorts people to live, and how it announces the things that happened to King Herod and the Jews and Pilate, your governor who was among them with his soldiers, against Christ, and that he was to be believed by people of every nation, and that God calls him Son and has promised to subject all enemies to him, and how demons, as far as they can, try to flee the power of the Father of all and the Lord Christ, and how God calls all to repentance before the day of judgment comes. It has been said thus: Blessed is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the ungodly and has not stood in the way of sinners and has not sat in the seat of the pestilential, but rather in the law of the Lord his will, and in the law of the Lord he will meditate day and night. And he will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, which will yield its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not wither, and all that he does will prosper. Not so the ungodly, not so, but like chaff, which the wind blows away from the face of the earth; therefore, the ungodly will not rise in judgment, nor sinners in the counsel of the righteous, because the Lord knows the way of the righteous, and the way of the ungodly will perish. Why have the nations raged and the peoples devised vain things? The kings of the earth have taken their stand, and the rulers have gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ, saying: Let us break their bonds and cast away their yoke from us. He who dwells in the heavens will laugh at them, and the Lord will mock them; then he will speak to them in his anger, and in his wrath he will disturb them. But I have been established as king by him on his holy mountain Zion, proclaiming the Lord's decree. The Lord said to me: You are my Son, today I have begotten you. Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession; you will shepherd them with an iron rod, as a potter's vessels you will shatter them. And now, kings, understand; all you who judge the earth, be instructed. Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice before him with trembling. Take hold of instruction, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the way of the righteous, when his wrath is kindled in a short time. Blessed are all who trust in him.

pass_b_english: Listen and consider how it was foretold, through the prophetic Spirit, by the prophet and king mentioned earlier, concerning those who would preach his teaching and announce his appearance: "Day after day pours forth speech, and night after night declares knowledge. There is no speech or language where their voice is not heard. Their sound has gone out through all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world" (Psalm 19:1-4). In the sun he has pitched his tent, and like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, he rejoices like a giant to run his course.

Beyond these words, we also judged it right to recall other prophecies spoken through the Spirit of David, from which you can learn how the prophetic Spirit urges people to live. It announces what happened to King Herod, the Jews, and Pilate, your governor among them with his soldiers, when they conspired against Christ. It declares that he was to be believed by people of every nation, that God calls him Son and has promised to subject all enemies to him, and that demons, as far as they are able, try to flee the authority of the Father of all, the Lord God, and of his Christ. It shows how God calls everyone to repentance before the day of judgment arrives.

These things were said as follows: "Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers; but his delight is in the law of the Lord, and on his law he meditates day and night. He will be like a tree planted by streams of water, yielding its fruit in season, its leaf never withering; everything he does will prosper. The wicked are not so, but are like chaff the wind drives from the face of the earth. Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous; for the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish" (Psalm 1:1-6).

"Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain? The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers gather together against the Lord and against his Anointed, saying, 'Let us break their bonds and cast their cords from us'" (Psalm 2:1-3). He who sits in the heavens laughs; the Lord holds them in derision. Then he will speak to them in his wrath and terrify them in his fury. "But I have been set as king by him on Zion, his holy hill, proclaiming the Lord's decree. The Lord said to me, 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you'" (Psalm 2:7). "Ask of me, and I will make the nations your inheritance, and the ends of the earth your possession. You will shepherd them with a rod of iron; you will shatter them like a potter's vessels" (Psalm 2:8-9).

Therefore now, O kings, be wise; be warned, all you who judge the earth. Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice with trembling. Take hold of discipline, lest the Lord be angry and you perish in the way, for his wrath is quickly kindled. Blessed are all who take refuge in him.

review.notes: Pass B fails on agency and accuracy regarding the Greek text. 1. In the clause 'καὶ τὴν αἰτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐξουσίαν φυγεῖν πειρῶνται', the Greek refers to the 'authority of the [air/heavenly one] of Christ' (noting the OCR/textual corruption 'αἰτοῦ' likely intended as 'αἰθέρος' or similar, but the translator must follow the provided text). Pass B translates this as 'the authority of the Father of all, the Lord God, and of his Christ', which adds 'the Father of all, the Lord God'—a significant addition of agency/identity not present in the Greek. 2. In the clause 'καὶ ὁ κύριος ἐκμυκτηριεῖ αὐτός', Pass B translates 'the Lord holds them in derision', whereas Pass A correctly identifies the verb 'ἐκμυκτηριεῖ' (to mock/deride). 3. In the clause 'καὶ ἐν τῷ θυμῷ αὐτοῦ ταράξει αὐτός', Pass B translates 'and terrify them in his fury', whereas Pass A correctly translates 'ταράξει' as 'disturb' (as noted in the lemmas). Pass B's 'terrify' is a departure from the Greek 'ταράξει'.
uncertainties: The term 'αἰτοῦ' in the Greek is likely a corruption/OCR error for 'αἰθέρος' or similar, but Pass B adds 'the Father of all, the Lord God' which is not in the source text.
reasons: Pass B adds 'the Father of all, the Lord God' to the phrase 'καὶ τὴν αἰτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐξουσίαν', which is not in the Greek.
Pass B translates 'ταράξει' as 'terrify', which contradicts the lemma/Pass A 'disturb'.
